articles.title: Top 5 small-cap funds can take 28 days longer than mid-caps to sell half of their portfolios: Experts discuss risks
articles.summary: SEBI’s FY26 data shows top five small-cap funds take 51 days to liquidate half their portfolios, versus 23 days for mid-caps. Experts say lower small-cap liquidity and rising AUM can increase redemption risks, making stress-test trends worth monitoring.

articles.title: Riding the wave: Active momentum funds beat market volatility — what’s the strategy?
articles.summary: Momentum strategies capitalise on market trends by purchasing ascending stocks while exiting underperforming names.

articles.title: Overseas equities or crypto: Where are Indian investors putting their money in 2026?
articles.summary: Indian investors are looking beyond domestic markets, with overseas equities and crypto both seeing strong participation. The data reveals that investors are using both as part of a broader diversification strategy.

articles.title: 8th Pay Commission: Govt gives status report in Lok Sabha; what employees should know
articles.summary: The government said the 8th Pay Commission was given 18 months from the date of its constitution to submit its report. Here's who could benefit and what remains undecided on salaries and pensions.

articles.title: Not all multi-asset allocation funds are alike: Only one scheme is rated low risk —why others are red-flagged
articles.summary: Multi-asset allocation funds may look similar, but their risk profiles can be poles apart. Of the 34 schemes, only one carries a Low risk rating, while five are rated High risk. The portfolio mix offers some clues.

articles.title: Repo rate stays at 5.25%: Why your home loan EMI may still change in 2026 and what historical data shows
articles.summary: Even if the RBI keeps the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in 2026, your home loan EMI may not stay the same. MCLR-linked loans can move independently, while even repo-linked loans may see changes. Historical data reveals an uneven link between the MCLR and policy rate.

articles.title: REIT, InvIT dividend tax relief may boost investor returns; know who benefits and what remains taxable
articles.summary: The proposed tax change could make REIT and InvIT dividends tax-free for investors regardless of the tax regime chosen by the underlying SPV. However, interest and other components of distributions will remain taxable, so investors must check the payout breakup before calculating post-tax returns.

articles.title: Ladli Behna Yojana MP: 39th instalment of ₹1,500 may arrive early as Raksha Bandhan gift
articles.summary: The Ladli Behna Yojana serves as a crucial pillar for economic empowerment, supplying eligible women across Madhya Pradesh with direct financial assistance of ₹1,500 every month.

articles.title: Received an income tax notice? Here's why you should authenticate it and how to do it online
articles.summary: Filed ITR for AY 2026-27 and received an income tax notice? Before responding, taxpayers can authenticate it online to check whether it was genuinely issued by the department. Here’s how the DIN and OTP-based verification can help you spot fake notices.

articles.title: Will you be charged for UPI peer transfers, grocery payments? MyGovIndia busts myths on MDR; here's what stays free
articles.summary: Viral claims suggest UPI payments could soon become chargeable after a recent PSS Act amendment. MyGovIndia has clarified that routine personal UPI transfers remain free. Here are the key myths and facts every UPI user should be aware of.

articles.title: Capital Gains Tax: How stocks, ETFs and equity mutual funds are taxed now
articles.summary: For equity mutual funds, exchange-traded funds and stocks, the holding period required to qualify as a long-term investment is more than 12 months. STCG on these assets is taxed at 20%, while LTCG is taxed at 12.5% on gains exceeding the applicable annual exemption threshold.

articles.title: Closing a credit card with outstanding EMI? Experts explain hidden charges and rules
articles.summary: Cancelling a credit card with an outstanding EMI does not erase repayment obligations. Know what happens to EMIs, foreclosure charges, pending dues and credit scores before closing your card.
